content:
4
オーケストレーション

1つのClaudeセッションが専門的な作業のために別のセッションに引き継ぐパイプラインを設計する。

例えば
「ブログ記事を書く」を1つのClaudeに頼むと、調べる・書く・チェックする・整える、全部混ざって雑になる。
そこで分業させる

①リサーチ担当Claude → ネタを調べてまとめるだけ
②下書き担当Claude → 1の情報をもとに文章を書くだけ
③レビュー担当Claude → 2の文章をチェック・修正するだけ
④公開担当Claude → 3を整えて投稿用に仕上げるだけ

前のClaudeの成果物を、次のClaudeに渡していく。工場のベルトコンベアみたいなイメージ。
「AIオーケストレーションエンジニア」というのは、この“Claudeたちの流れ”を設計する人のこと

content:
『Gemini』の動画生成能力が強すぎる
適当なプロンプトでこの精度
5歳児でも動画クリエイターになれる時代
なぜこんなにもリアルに作れるのか
仕組みは　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　

Veoモデルの力:
現在の動画生成には、
Googleが開発した『Veo 3』
または『Veo 3.1 Fast』という
非常に高度なAIモデルを使用している。
これらのモデルは、膨大な量の
映像データとテキストデータを
学習しており、現実世界の物理法則
（光の反射、影の動き、重力など）や、
様々な物体がどのように動くか
を深く理解している。

テキストからの理解と構築:
皆さんが入力したプロンプトを、
AIが詳細に解析する。
日本の絶景という言葉から、
山、海、空、季節感、光の当たり方など、
映像に必要な要素をすべて計算し、
ピクセル単位で映像を一から構築していく。

高度なシネマティックコントロール:
この技術は単に画像を動かすだけでなく、
カメラワーク、被写界深度、
アスペクト比など、
映画のような映像を作るための要素も
精密に制御できる。
これにより、よりプロフェッショナルで
リアルな仕上がりになる。

一貫性の保持:
動画として破綻しないよう、
フレームごとの繋がりを
非常に滑らかに計算している。
そのため、物が突然消えたり形が
変わったりすることなく、
自然な動きを表現できる。

title: Gemini Omniで動画生成はどう変わったのか？重要ポイントだけ解説
content:
Google Geminiの新しい動画生成モデル「Gemini Omni」が登場！
（YouTube動画でも解説しましたので、見たい方はこちらから視聴できます）
Gemini Omniは、動画内のテキスト表現が大きく進化しています。
これまでAI動画では、文字が崩れたり、日本語がうまく表示されなかったりすることが多かったですが、今回のモデルでは日本語テキストもかなり綺麗に表示できるようになっています。
例えば「AI動画の文字が進化、もう崩れない？、のテキストを乗せた動画を作って」と雑な指示で作った動画が下記です。
このレベルでテキストを綺麗に生成できるようになってました。
最大のポイントは、短い文字や固定されたテキストを動画内に入れる精度がかなり高いことです。たとえば、タイトル風の文字、字幕、簡単な説明テキストなどはかなり実用的なレベルになっています。
若干音声が気になる部分はありますが、SNS動画、YouTubeショート、広告風の動画、解説アニメなどに使いやすそうです。
一方で、まだ苦手な部分もあります。リアルタイムで文字を書いていく表現や、細かい文字が大量に並ぶデザインは崩れやすく、完全に安定しているわけではありません。
下記の例は「こんにちはと文字を書く」と指示して生成した動画。
現状は、1〜2行くらいの大きめな文字を固定して見せる用途が一番向いています。
そして、もう一つ面白い進化が、動画を入力素材として使える点です。
撮影済みの動画をもとに、アニメ風、白黒線画、油絵風、漫画風などへ変換できます。元動画の動きや構図を活かしながら、雰囲気だけを大きく変えられるので、ショート動画の演出としてかなり相性が良さそうです。
下記の例はYouTube動画の一シーンを素材にしてみたものです。
ただし、音声はまだ微妙な部分があります。
映像だけをGemini Omniで変換し、音声は元動画のものを編集で重ねる、という使い方が現実的です。
最後に注意点としては、著作物に近いキャラクターや既存作品っぽい表現が出てしまう可能性があることです。商用利用や公開前提の動画では、意図せず既存キャラクターに寄っていないか確認する必要があります。
まとめると、Gemini Omniはまだガチャ要素はあるものの、「文字入りAI動画」を作る力がかなり実用段階に近づいたモデルです。特に、短い日本語テキスト、字幕付き解説動画、元動画のスタイル変換には大きな可能性があります。
他にも色々面白い事例があったらSubstackのオープンチャットで共有していきます。あとOmni専用Gemも作成したので、それも併せてオープンチャットで共有しておきます。

title:
架空のゲーム『HOLLOW HOLLOW』のトレーラーを、エージェントと一緒に制作しました。

今回見てほしいのは映像そのものより、制作プロセスです。

明確な完成イメージがない状態から、

・世界観の方向性
・カット構成
・映像生成
・編集
・音入れ

content:
⑧ Googleから「AP2」が登場。

AP2はAgent Payments Protocolの略で、
AIエージェントが安全に代理決済するための仕組み。

ポイントは、AIが勝手に買うのではなく、
ユーザーが決めた条件の範囲内でだけ購入できること。

・ブランドを指定
・商品を指定
・予算を指定
・条件一致時だけ購入を実行
・決済情報や個人データを保護
・デジタル委任状で本人代理を証明
・返品時に使える取引記録も残る

これまでAIは「提案する」までだったが、
いよいよ「購入する」領域に入ってきた。

AIエージェント時代、決済プロトコルを誰が握るかはかなり重要。

Googleがここを取りに来たのは大きい。

APIコストを気にせず、ノートPCなどの限られたリソースでも爆速でコーディング補助を受けられます。
ローカル完結なので機密コードの取り扱いも安心。MITライセンスでGitHubに公開されており、今後の開発エージェントの常識を変えるかもしれません！🚀

GPT-5.5 / Claude Opus 4.7 / Seedance / Veo / Kling が
『1本のシネマティック制作ライン』として自動で繋がる仕組み！！

どこがエグいのか整理します👇

これまで

でしたが——

その前提、Higgsfield側から崩しに来ました。

【今回のSupercomputerで何が変わった？】

シーンごとに違う動画モデルを
自動で振り分けて1本に繋いでくれます。

つまり👇
・脚本と演出はGPT-5.5やClaude Opus 4.7に書かせる
・カメラワーク重めのカットはSeedanceに送る
・実写質感の表情はVeoに送る
・派手なモーションはKlingに送る

【使い方（拍子抜けするほど簡単）】

① 作りたい映像の演出を1行で書く
② Supercomputerが必要なモデルを自動選定
③ シーンごとにベストモデルで生成
④ Higgsfield側で1本のタイムラインに統合

これで
「考える → 指示する → 完パケが上がる」 が
ほぼ手元で完結します。

映像制作を
「コストが重い」で止めていた個人ほど、
今回の機能は本気で触る価値あります。

モデル単体じゃなく『組み合わせて指揮するハブ』として捉える発想は、Claude Code＋MCPサーバー側でも同じ流れになってる。

content:
Claude Codeのagent view、エンジニアだけの話に見えて普通にマーケ側も関係あります。

公式が出してる新機能で、複数のClaude Codeセッションを一画面で見て、作業中、入力待ち、完了、失敗をまとめて管理する流れ。

今までAI活用って、1個投げる、終わる、確認する、また投げる、みたいな使い方が多かった。

でもこれからは、複数のAIタスクを同時に走らせて、人間が進行を見る形に寄っていくと思ってます。

僕の文脈で言うなら、

リサーチ。
企画。
執筆。
レビュー。
投稿準備。

このへんを1個ずつ投げるより、工程ごとに走らせて最後に人間が見るイメージ。

月30時間かけてたコンテンツ制作が5時間になったのも、結局は作業を工程に分けてAIに渡したからです。

複数走らせるほど速くなる。

でも雑に走らせると、ズレた作業も同時に量産される。

🥺「AIを増やせば全部終わります！」

これは絶対にやっちゃダメです。

増やす前に決めるべきなのは、

・どこまでAIに渡すか
・どこで人間が止めるか
・何を見たらOKにするか
・失敗した時にどこへ戻すか

このへん。

AIを1体使う時代から、複数のAIタスクを見ながら判断する時代へ。

content:
“Claude Code for Marketing” sounds like a meme at first.

until you realize that’s literally where the internet is heading.

one prompt: Claude understands your product, finds winning angles, generates hooks, creates short-form content, and ships distribution faster than entire marketing teams.

that’s why the Fastlane launch blew up.

not because people suddenly care about “AI marketing tools”

people care about leverage.

the launch tapped into a very specific founder fantasy:

> “what if growth felt like running a command?”

and they packaged that feeling perfectly.

terminal UI. minimal copy. one absurd promise.

“Ship 30 days of viral content in 30 seconds.”

that line alone explains why the post crossed millions of views.

because great marketing today is not about sounding corporate.

it’s about compressing possibility into one sentence.

and honestly, the smartest thing they did was attaching themselves to the Claude Code vibe.

developers already associate Claude Code with: speed, automation, shipping, operator energy.

so when you say: “Claude Code for Marketing”

people instantly understand the positioning without needing a 5-minute explanation.

that’s elite distribution psychology.

the deeper shift here is this:

marketing is turning into infrastructure.

the best teams are no longer asking: “how do we make content?”

they’re asking: “how do we build systems that generate attention every day?”

huge difference.

because attention now compounds like software.

the faster you test, the faster you learn.

the faster you learn, the faster you grow.

AI didn’t create this shift.

AI just removed the friction.

and the teams that understand this early are going to dominate distribution for the next few years.

You've been using Claude for months.

And you're still copy-pasting the same context every single chat.

That's not a Claude problem. That's a setup problem.

Most people use Claude like a search engine.
Type. Get answer. Close tab. Repeat.

Top operators? They built a system.
And the whole system runs on 4 files.

Here's exactly how it works 👇

① CLAUDE.md — Your Foundation

Claude starts every chat with zero memory of you.
No preferences. No brand voice. No idea how you work.

CLAUDE.md fixes that.

It's one file Claude reads before every conversation.
Your brand rules. Your workflow. Your non-negotiables.
All loaded automatically — every single time.

Think of it as the onboarding doc for your best employee.
Except this employee never forgets what's in it.

What goes inside:
— How you write (tone, style, what you hate)
— Workflow rules ("plan before you execute")
— What Claude should NEVER do in your chats

Every time Claude gets something wrong → don't just fix the output. Fix the brief. Update the file. Make the mistake impossible next time.

② memory/ folder — Claude Remembers

Every correction, preference, and rule you've ever given Claude?
Gone. Next session, you start over.

Not anymore.

You can tell Claude to save anything as a memory file.
It creates a .md file in your memory/ folder.
It loads that file in every future session.

"Remember I never use bullet points in captions."
Done. Forever. Never say it again.

The real power move: after every strategy call or important decision, tell Claude to summarize and save it. Your entire business context — always in the room.

③ Skills — Your Custom Commands

Every time you write the same prompt twice, that's a problem.
Skills solve it permanently.

A skill is a reusable workflow you fire with one command.

/create → writes a post in your exact voice
/today → pulls calendar + inbox, plans your day
/repurpose → one post becomes 5 formats
/brief → messy notes become a clean scope doc

You describe what it should do.
Claude builds the SKILL.md file.
You fire it from any chat, any project, any time.

One hour of setup. Hundreds of hours saved.

④ Agents — Your Dream Team

This is where it gets serious.

An agent is Claude with one specific job.
A pipeline is multiple agents handing work off in sequence.

Example — content pipeline:
Strategist → picks the angle
Writer → drafts the piece
Editor → cuts and sharpens
QA Scorer → grades against your standards
Publisher → formats and sends

You give one instruction at the top.
The pipeline delivers a finished output at the bottom.
You didn't touch anything in the middle.

Use Opus for judgment and strategy.
Use Sonnet for execution and speed.
Right model, right job, every time.

THE CLOSE:

4 files. That's it.

Context. Memory. Skills. Agents.

This isn't about prompting better.
It's about building a machine that runs without you.

The people getting 10x results from Claude aren't smarter.
They just stopped treating it like a chatbot

content:
holy shit.

Someone just open-sourced a diagnostic that runs 32 inspections on any AI agent and tells you exactly where it's misaligned.

It's called iFixAi. You point it at OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, or your own agent. Five minutes later you get a scorecard graded A through F across five categories of misalignment risk.

The five categories it tests for:

→ FABRICATION: tool authorization leaks, missing audit trails, unsourced claims, overconfident responses
→ MANIPULATION: hallucination, privilege escalation, prompt injection, malicious deployer rules
→ DECEPTION: evaluation-awareness sandbagging, covert side tasks, long-horizon drift, goal stability
→ UNPREDICTABILITY: context distortion, instruction drift, decision stability across runs
→ OPACITY: regulatory readiness, session leakage, training-contamination attestation, escalation paths

Two mandatory minimums are baked in. Tool authorization must hit 100%. Privilege escalation must hit 95%. Fail either one and your overall score gets capped at 60% no matter how well you did everywhere else.

Every run writes a content-addressed manifest that captures every input. So you can drop it into CI, track drift over weeks, and prove your agent isn't quietly degrading between deploys.

The Full mode is what makes it serious. You bring two different judge providers and it runs a multi-judge ensemble with conservative tie-break and per-judge attribution. No silent self-judging. If you only have one credential, the run literally refuses to compare systems for you.

Industry agnostic by design. The test code is domain-neutral. Healthcare, customer support, software engineering knowledge lives in fixture YAML you write yourself. Three example fixtures ship in the repo.

It also maps every test to OWASP LLM Top 10, NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act, and ISO 42001. One flag and you get a regulatory gap analysis.

Built by @ifixai_ai.

Apache 2.0. 100% Opensource.

title: Claude Just Turned Job Hunting Into a Prompt
content:
For years, the internet made job hunting feel broken.

Thousands of listings.
Hundreds of applications.
Endless resume edits.
Ghost recruiters.
ATS filters.
Fake networking.
Keyword games.

People weren’t getting hired based on talent anymore.

They were getting hired based on who could survive the system.

And honestly?

Most of the “career industry” existed because the internet became too noisy to navigate alone.

Recruiters filtered opportunities.
Resume consultants optimized wording.
Career coaches helped with positioning.
Sourcers matched candidates to companies.

Entire businesses were built around helping humans deal with information overload.

Then Claude connected to the internet.

And suddenly…

the workflow changed.

This is the moment people underestimate.

Most people still think Claude is:

- a chatbot
- a writing tool
- an AI assistant

But that framing is already outdated.

Claude is quietly becoming an execution layer for the internet itself.

Not just answering questions.

Actually doing work.

And once you connect it to tools like Apify, the entire recruiting workflow starts collapsing into one conversation.

Here’s what’s crazy.

You can literally upload your resume into Claude and say:

«“Based on my experience, find the highest-paying jobs I actually qualify for.”»

That’s it.

Claude:

- reads your resume
- understands your background
- searches live listings across the internet
- filters irrelevant roles
- ranks opportunities by fit
- identifies compensation ranges
- explains why specific roles match your experience

In seconds.

Not after 3 weeks of applications.

Not after paying a recruiter.

Not after manually searching LinkedIn for hours.

One prompt.

That should terrify a lot of industries.

But this is only the surface-level use case.

The real breakthrough is contextual understanding.

Claude doesn’t just scan resumes.

It understands positioning.

That changes everything.

Because the same experience can be framed in completely different ways depending on the opportunity.

Example:

One company sees:

«“content creator”»

Another sees:

«“growth strategist”»

Another sees:

«“AI-native distribution operator”»

Same person.
Different framing.
Different outcome.

Humans used to manually optimize this process.

Now Claude can do it instantly.

And probably more effectively than most people.

The recruiting industry was built on asymmetry.

Recruiters had:

- information access
- filtering systems
- hiring insights
- network advantages

Candidates had:

- confusion
- guesswork
- anxiety

AI destroys that asymmetry.

Because now the candidate has:

- internet-scale search
- reasoning
- personalization
- optimization
- strategic guidance

inside one chat window.

That’s the shift.

And this doesn’t stop at job discovery.

This is where it gets absurd.

After Claude finds the role, you can say:

«“Tailor my resume for this exact position.”»

And it rewrites:

- keywords
- achievements
- framing
- narrative
- positioning
- project descriptions

specifically around that company’s job description.

Not generic resume advice.

Actual contextual optimization.

Then you can say:

«“Prepare me for the interview.”»

And Claude:

- researches the company
- predicts likely interview questions
- analyzes the role requirements
- generates strategic answers
- identifies weak spots in your experience
- prepares negotiation talking points

At this point…

you’re not using AI as a tool anymore.

You’re using it like an autonomous career operating system.

That’s why recruiters are panicking.

Because the valuable part of recruiting was never “sending job links.”

It was:

- filtering
- ranking
- positioning
- understanding fit
- reducing uncertainty

Claude now does all five.

At internet scale.

24/7.

With near-zero friction.

And it keeps improving every month.

Most people still haven’t realized what’s happening.

The internet is shifting from:

information retrieval

to

intelligent execution

Search engines gave you options.

AI gives you outcomes.

That’s a completely different paradigm.

And once people understand this…

entire workflows disappear.

Not because humans vanish.

But because AI compresses layers of coordination into software.

One person with Claude now has leverage that previously required:

- recruiters
- assistants
- researchers
- analysts
- coordinators

That leverage gap is about to become enormous.

The craziest part?

This is still primitive.

Right now humans are still directing the workflow.

Soon the workflow will direct itself.

Imagine this:

Claude continuously monitors the internet for matching roles.

When a new opportunity appears:

- it analyzes fit
- updates your resume automatically
- drafts outreach
- prepares applications
- researches the company
- tracks responses
- schedules follow-ups
- optimizes your positioning over time

before you even wake up.

That’s not science fiction anymore.

That’s where this is heading.

Fast.

The biggest career advantage in the next decade won’t be your degree.

It won’t even be your network.

It’ll be your ability to build systems around intelligence.

Because the people winning in the AI era won’t necessarily be:

- the smartest
- the most experienced
- the most talented

They’ll be the ones who understand leverage first.

And Claude might end up becoming one of the biggest leverage tools ever created for individual workers.

Not because it replaced humans.

But because it replaced friction.

content:
AI-generated code is about to create a new kind of technical debt:

Database chaos.

Not bad UI.
Not buggy frontend code.

I’m talking about:
• broken migrations
• conflicting schema changes
• agents overwriting production data
• preview environments sharing the same database
• “it worked locally” at AI speed

That’s the layer Netlify just attacked with their new Database launch.

And honestly?

This is one of the first launches that actually feels designed for the AI-agent era instead of simply adding “AI” to existing infrastructure.

Here’s the shift:

Every AI run can now get:
→ its own isolated Postgres branch
→ its own migrations
→ its own preview environment
→ its own test data

So Claude Code, Codex, or Gemini can experiment freely without touching production.

That sounds small until you realize what’s happening across development right now:

One engineer is no longer making 3–4 changes a day.

AI agents are generating:

- entire backend systems
- database schemas
- migrations
- previews
- feature branches

…in minutes.

Traditional infra was never built for this volume of experimentation.

@Netlify basically combined:
• Deploy Previews
• Git-style workflows
• Postgres branching
• AI agent orchestration

into one developer workflow.

The smartest part?

They didn’t try reinventing databases.

Still Postgres.
Still migration-based.
Still works with Drizzle/ORM workflows developers already use.

But now the infrastructure matches how modern builders actually work.

This is the kind of launch that won’t go viral outside developer circles…

yet quietly changes how AI products get shipped over the next few years.

title: 9 Claude Code Plugins That Make It Feel Like You Hired a Senior Engineer
content:
Most people use Claude Code like a chatbot.

Smart ones use it like a coding copilot.

But power users?

They turn Claude into a fully equipped AI engineering system with plugins that:
• debug code faster
• search huge codebases instantly
• generate production-ready UI
• automate boring workflows
• connect directly with GitHub, terminals, databases, docs, and APIs

That’s where Claude Code becomes unfair.

Here are the best Claude Code plugins/tools that actually change how you build software 👇

1. Context7 — Gives Claude Real Documentation Context

One of the biggest problems with AI coding:

Outdated documentation.

Context7 fixes that by feeding Claude the latest framework and library docs directly inside the workflow.

So instead of hallucinating:
• old React syntax
• deprecated APIs
• outdated package structures

Claude works with fresh context.

This becomes insanely useful for:
• Next.js
• Supabase
• LangChain
• Stripe
• Vercel AI SDK
• Tailwind
• OpenAI SDKs

Why it matters:

The quality of AI output depends on the quality of context.

Context7 massively upgrades that context layer.

2. GitHub MCP — Turns Claude Into a GitHub Operator

This one feels futuristic.

Claude can:
• read repos
• review PRs
• inspect issues
• summarize commits
• understand project architecture
• generate fixes from GitHub context

Instead of manually pasting files into chat, Claude can understand the entire repo structure.

This changes everything for:
• debugging
• onboarding
• large projects
• open-source contribution
• code reviews

It feels less like prompting.

And more like working with an actual engineer.

3. Playwright MCP — AI That Can Actually Use Your App

Most AI tools can write frontend code.

Very few can test it properly.

Playwright MCP allows Claude to:
• open browsers
• click buttons
• test flows
• inspect UI issues
• reproduce bugs
• validate fixes automatically

This is where AI coding starts becoming autonomous.

You can literally say:

“Find why the signup flow breaks on mobile.”

And Claude can investigate the issue step by step.

Huge shift.

4. Filesystem MCP — Gives Claude Full Project Awareness

Without filesystem access, AI is basically blind.

With filesystem plugins:
Claude can:
• navigate folders
• read multiple files
• refactor entire projects
• trace dependencies
• understand architecture

This dramatically improves:
• refactoring
• debugging
• migrations
• cleanup tasks
• large-scale edits

The difference is massive.

Small context AI = assistant
Full repo context AI = teammate

5. Sequential Thinking — Makes Claude Think Like an Engineer

This is one of the most underrated tools.

Instead of jumping to answers instantly, Sequential Thinking forces Claude to:
• break problems into steps
• reason through architecture
• evaluate alternatives
• debug logically
• avoid shallow outputs

This dramatically improves:
• system design
• backend logic
• debugging
• agent workflows
• infrastructure planning

You get fewer “AI guesses.”

And more real engineering reasoning.

6. Browser Tools MCP — Real-Time Web Access For Coding

This plugin is insanely useful.

Claude can:
• search documentation
• inspect websites
• analyze APIs
• read technical articles
• compare implementations
• gather live information

This matters because coding changes weekly now.

Static training data is no longer enough.

The best AI workflows combine:
• reasoning
• tooling
• live context
• execution

That’s the real future.

7. Database MCP — Query Databases Directly

This is where things become dangerous in a good way.

Claude can:
• inspect schemas
• run queries
• debug database issues
• analyze relationships
• generate migrations
• optimize SQL

For developers working with:
• Postgres
• Supabase
• MySQL
• SQLite

This saves ridiculous amounts of time.

Especially during debugging sessions.

8. Terminal Access — The Biggest Upgrade Of Them All

Once Claude gets terminal access, everything changes.

Now it can:
• install packages
• run tests
• start servers
• execute scripts
• debug runtime issues
• automate workflows

This is the point where AI stops being “chat.”

And starts becoming infrastructure.

You’re no longer asking for code.

You’re orchestrating execution.

9. Memory Plugins — The Missing Layer Most People Ignore

Most AI sessions forget everything.

Memory plugins change that.

Claude can remember:
• project decisions
• architecture patterns
• coding preferences
• workflow rules
• ongoing tasks

This makes long-term collaboration dramatically better.

Instead of repeating context every session, Claude evolves with the project.

That’s a huge unlock.

The Big Shift Most Developers Haven’t Realized Yet

The future of AI coding is NOT better prompting.

It’s better tooling.

The winners won’t be people who ask AI random questions.

The winners will be developers who build high-context AI environments.

That means combining:
• memory
• repos
• terminals
• browsers
• databases
• documentation
• reasoning systems

Into one workflow.

That’s when Claude stops acting like ChatGPT.

And starts acting like an AI engineering teammate.

Most people are still using AI like autocomplete.

Meanwhile power users are building entire software systems with it.

Huge difference.

And we’re still early.

1. Context7 — Gives Claude Real Documentation Context

One of the biggest problems with AI coding:

Outdated documentation.

Context7 fixes that by feeding Claude the latest framework and library docs directly inside the workflow.

So instead of hallucinating:
• old React syntax
• deprecated APIs
• outdated package structures

Claude works with fresh context.

This becomes insanely useful for:
• Next.js

• LangChain
• Stripe

The quality of AI output depends on the quality of context.

Context7 massively upgrades that context layer.

2. GitHub MCP — Turns Claude Into a GitHub Operator

Claude can:
• read repos
• review PRs
• inspect issues
• summarize commits
• understand project architecture

Instead of manually pasting files into chat, Claude can understand the entire repo structure.

This changes everything for:
• debugging
• onboarding
• large projects
• open-source contribution
• code reviews

It feels less like prompting.

And more like working with an actual engineer.

3. Playwright MCP — AI That Can Actually Use Your App

Very few can test it properly.

Playwright MCP allows Claude to:
• open browsers
• click buttons
• test flows
• inspect UI issues
• reproduce bugs
• validate fixes automatically

This is where AI coding starts becoming autonomous.

You can literally say:

“Find why the signup flow breaks on mobile.”

And Claude can investigate the issue step by step.

Huge shift.

4. Filesystem MCP — Gives Claude Full Project Awareness

Without filesystem access, AI is basically blind.

With filesystem plugins:
Claude can:
• navigate folders
• read multiple files
• refactor entire projects
• trace dependencies
• understand architecture

This dramatically improves:
• refactoring
• debugging
• migrations
• cleanup tasks
• large-scale edits

The difference is massive.

Small context AI = assistant
Full repo context AI = teammate

5. Sequential Thinking — Makes Claude Think Like an Engineer

This is one of the most underrated tools.

Instead of jumping to answers instantly, Sequential Thinking forces Claude to:
• break problems into steps
• reason through architecture
• evaluate alternatives
• debug logically
• avoid shallow outputs

This dramatically improves:
• system design
• backend logic

You get fewer “AI guesses.”

And more real engineering reasoning.

6. Browser Tools MCP — Real-Time Web Access For Coding

This plugin is insanely useful.

Claude can:

This matters because coding changes weekly now.

Static training data is no longer enough.

That’s the real future.

7. Database MCP — Query Databases Directly

For developers working with:

• execute scripts
• debug runtime issues
• automate workflows

This is the point where AI stops being “chat.”

And starts becoming infrastructure.

9. Memory Plugins — The Missing Layer Most People Ignore

Most AI sessions forget everything.

Memory plugins change that.

Claude can remember:

• coding preferences
• workflow rules
• ongoing tasks

This makes long-term collaboration dramatically better.

Instead of repeating context every session, Claude evolves with the project.

That’s a huge unlock.

The Big Shift Most Developers Haven’t Realized Yet

The future of AI coding is NOT better prompting.

content:
Most teams are building MCP servers the same way people built internal tools in 2019:

one endpoint = one tool

Then six months later the agent has 47 tools, picks the wrong one half the time, burns tokens routing requests, and nobody knows why latency exploded.

The interesting part about MCP isn’t “agents using tools.”

It’s that MCP quietly introduced a new application architecture layer for AI systems.

And most people still treat it like glorified API wrappers.

The real shift:

• Some MCP servers should expose actions
• Some should expose context
• Some should orchestrate workflows
• Some should maintain state
• Some should literally behave like agents

Those are completely different design patterns.

Example:

A GitHub MCP and a Playwright MCP should not be designed the same way.

One is basically stateless API access.

The other is managing a live browser session, state, retries, cleanup, auth, memory leaks, and continuity across calls.

Same protocol. Completely different architecture problem.

That’s the mistake I keep seeing:

Teams choosing MCP patterns based on what’s easiest to implement…

instead of what minimizes context load, tool confusion, latency, and orchestration overhead for the model.

The best AI infra people I know are starting to think about MCP servers less like “tools”

and more like:

• execution environments
• context systems
• workflow runtimes
• delegated reasoning units

That mental shift changes everything.

The biggest unlock for me personally:

“Should this be a tool call… or should this entire workflow disappear behind the MCP layer?”

That single decision affects reliability more than the model itself.

title: The Real Power of Claude Code Starts When You Stop “Prompting”
content:
Stop Writing Better Prompts. Start Designing Better Systems.

Most developers are still using Claude Code like it’s a smarter autocomplete.

They open a session.
Write a prompt.
Hope the output works.
Retry if it fails.
Get frustrated when the second attempt is worse than the first.

And honestly?

That workflow completely misses the point of Claude Code.

The real shift happening right now isn’t “AI writes code.”

The real shift is that software development is slowly becoming system orchestration.

That sounds abstract until you see the difference in practice.

A beginner opens Claude and says:

“Build authentication for my app.”

An advanced builder creates:

• architecture context
• memory systems
• reasoning constraints
• validation loops
• reusable workflows
• automated refinement

One gets random outputs.

The other gets consistent engineering leverage.

That’s the gap.

And that gap is becoming bigger every month.

The Biggest Misconception About Claude Code

Most people think success with Claude comes from:

• writing better prompts
• finding secret keywords
• learning prompt engineering tricks

But after using Claude Code heavily, I realized something important:

Prompting is the smallest part of the workflow.

The real advantage comes from designing environments where Claude consistently performs well.

That’s why two developers can use the same model and get completely different results.

One feels like:

“AI is overhyped.”

The other feels like:

“This thing is changing how I build software.”

Same model.

Different system.

Prompts Are Temporary. Systems Compound.

Here’s what most AI workflows look like today:

Prompt → Output → Manual Fixes

That works for simple tasks.

But the moment projects become larger:

• outputs become inconsistent
• context gets messy
• bugs multiply
• architecture drifts
• Claude forgets important decisions

This is exactly where systems matter.

A real Claude workflow looks more like this:

Context → Constraints → Reasoning → Execution → Validation → Memory → Refinement

Once you operate this way, Claude stops feeling like a chatbot.

It starts feeling like an actual engineering environment.

Why Most Claude Outputs Feel Inconsistent

The answer is surprisingly simple:

Most developers provide terrible context.

And Claude can only reason using the environment you give it.

If your instructions are vague:

vague outputs

If your architecture is unclear:

messy implementations

If your project rules constantly change:

inconsistent code

The highest-leverage improvement you can make is not better prompting.

It’s better context engineering.

The best Claude users are extremely intentional about:

• project memory
• architecture constraints
• reusable instructions
• workflow consistency
• feedback systems

That’s what creates reliable outputs.

The Shift From “Prompting” to “Workflow Design”

This is the part most people haven’t realized yet.

The future AI-native developer probably won’t spend most of their time:

• typing code
• fixing syntax
• rewriting boilerplate

They’ll spend more time:

• defining systems
• orchestrating reasoning
• designing workflows
• managing context
• validating outputs

In other words:

The valuable skill is shifting from execution → orchestration.

That’s why some developers suddenly look unrealistically productive.

They aren’t individually doing 10x more work manually.

They’ve built systems that multiply output.

The Developers Getting Massive Results All Do This One Thing

They force structure before generation.

This is huge.

Beginners ask Claude:

“Build this feature.”

Advanced users force Claude to:

1. analyze the problem
2. identify edge cases
3. explain tradeoffs
4. define architecture decisions
5. propose implementation strategy
6. THEN generate code

That single change dramatically improves:

• reasoning quality
• architecture consistency
• maintainability
• debugging speed
• edge-case handling

Because the problem with AI-generated code usually isn’t syntax.

It’s poor thinking.

And if you don’t guide the reasoning process…

you debug the consequences later.

Feedback Loops Are Where Claude Becomes Dangerous

This is probably the biggest unlock.

Most people still use AI linearly:

generate → manually review

But advanced workflows create loops:

generate → test → analyze → refine → repeat

That changes everything.

Because once Claude can:

• inspect failures
• analyze outputs
• refine implementations
• iterate automatically

…the workflow starts compounding.

This is where AI stops behaving like a tool.

And starts behaving like an engineering system.

A lot of developers still haven’t experienced this yet.

But once you do, normal development workflows start feeling incredibly slow.

Constraints Actually Improve Creativity

This sounds counterintuitive at first.

Different system.

Prompt → Output → Manual Fixes

• bugs multiply
• architecture drifts

title: These 40 Claude Code Practices Made Me 10x More Productive Overnight
content:
I wasted months using Claude Code the wrong way.

I thought the tool itself was the advantage.

It wasn’t.

The real advantage was learning how to build a system around it.

Most people still use Claude Code like this:

“Write this function.”
“Fix this bug.”
“Explain this error.”

But the best engineers?

They use it like an autonomous operating system for development.

That shift changes everything.

Instead of coding faster…
you start thinking faster.

Instead of asking better prompts…
you start building better workflows.

And once that clicks, Claude Code stops feeling like an AI assistant.

It starts feeling like a second engineering brain.

Here are 40 Claude Code practices that genuinely changed how I work:

—

1. Stop using the full "claude" command every time.

Set up a simple alias like "cc" and remove unnecessary friction from your workflow. Tiny optimizations compound hard when you use the tool daily.

2. Treat permissions carefully — but remove repetitive approvals.

Constant confirmation popups destroy flow state. Power users automate trusted actions so they can stay focused on building instead of babysitting the terminal.

3. Add a live status line.

Seeing your branch, directory, and context usage in real time sounds small until you experience how much mental overhead it removes during long sessions.

4. Don’t blindly max out context windows.

A bigger context window doesn’t always mean better output. Learn when large context helps and when it silently reduces focus and precision.

5. Configure Claude’s writing style once.

Most people rewrite responses manually every session. Smart users define tone, verbosity, and formatting upfront so outputs stay consistent automatically.

6. Use remote control from your phone.

Starting a long-running task on your machine and checking progress remotely genuinely feels futuristic once it becomes part of your workflow.

7. Feed terminal output directly into Claude.

Instead of copying logs manually, pipe commands directly into context. This massively improves debugging speed and removes unnecessary back-and-forth.

8. Learn to stop bad generations early.

One underrated skill is recognizing when Claude is going in the wrong direction within the first 20 seconds instead of wasting 20 minutes.

9. Use rewind aggressively.

Experienced users rewind sessions constantly. They don’t force bad context chains to work. They reset fast and move forward cleaner.

10. Save unfinished prompts.

Complex prompts often evolve while thinking. Being able to stash drafts without losing your train of thought makes multi-step work dramatically smoother.

—

11. Run long tasks in the background.

Your AI should work while you think — not force you to sit idle waiting for builds and tests to finish.

12. Separate side questions from main workflows.

Advanced users protect their main context carefully. Small unrelated questions slowly poison long technical sessions if you let them pile up.

13. Use voice prompts for complex instructions.

When speaking naturally, you usually provide more nuance, edge cases, and constraints than when typing quickly.

14. Clear sessions more often than you think.

Most output quality degradation comes from messy accumulated context, not model intelligence.

15. Stop over-explaining bugs.

Raw logs are infinitely more valuable than emotional descriptions of problems.

16. Restart after repeated failed corrections.

If Claude misunderstands something twice, the session is usually already contaminated.

17. Use planning mode before large refactors.

The best builders spend more time shaping execution than fixing bad execution later.

18. Point Claude toward exact files.

Don’t waste tokens making it search your entire codebase for context you already know.

19. Use broad prompts to audit unfamiliar code.

Questions like:
“What feels wrong here?”
often uncover problems you never would’ve explicitly searched for.

20. Guide compaction manually.

Compression without direction loses critical context. Compression with intent preserves exactly what matters.

—

21. Use “ultrathink” only when complexity actually demands it.

Not every task needs maximum reasoning. Knowing when deep reasoning matters is part of becoming efficient.

22. Force Claude to verify its own work.

The single biggest quality jump happens when you make Claude run tests before calling something complete.

23. Install proper LSP support.

Automatic diagnostics create a feedback loop where Claude catches many issues before you ever see them.

24. Prefer lightweight CLI tools when possible.

Heavy integrations sound impressive but often waste context and increase noise.

25. Start with only a few MCP servers.

Most people overload their environment immediately. High-leverage users keep systems minimal and intentional.

26. Automate recurring checks.

Deployment monitoring, test watching, and background verification should happen automatically instead of consuming mental bandwidth.

27. Remove repetitive approvals.

Tiny interruptions kill deep work more than people realize.

28. Keep CLAUDE.md brutally lean.

Most instruction files are bloated with useless rules that dilute important guidance.

29. Every rule should prevent a real mistake.

If an instruction doesn’t change behavior meaningfully, it probably shouldn’t exist.

30. Continuously evolve your system.

Every repeated mistake should improve your workflow permanently.

—

31. Use conditional rules instead of global clutter.

Only load relevant instructions when needed. Context efficiency matters more than people think.

32. Reference external docs instead of pasting everything inline.

Smart context management is one of the biggest differences between average and elite Claude users.

33. Use Skills as modular knowledge systems.

Skills let you extend capability without bloating your baseline context.

34. Use hooks for non-negotiable requirements.

Suggestions are optional.
Hooks are enforcement.

That distinction matters.

35. Automate formatting completely.

Anything repetitive should disappear from your cognitive load.

36. Block dangerous commands automatically.

The safest workflows are usually the fastest because they allow higher autonomy confidently.

37. Use worktrees for parallel execution.

Running multiple isolated feature branches simultaneously changes how fast large projects move.

38. Use subagents to protect your main context.

Think of subagents like disposable research workers that report back without polluting your primary session.

39. Build specialized agents for recurring workflows.

Once you create reusable agents, you stop solving the same coordination problems repeatedly.

40. Experiment inside isolated sandboxes.

The best way to move faster is removing fear from experimentation.

—

Most people think AI coding tools are about writing code faster.

That’s surface-level thinking.

The real shift is this:

You stop acting like a solo engineer.

And start acting like someone managing an AI engineering system.

That’s where the leverage is.

That’s why some developers suddenly look 10x faster than everyone else.

It’s not because they type faster.

It’s because they’ve learned how to orchestrate intelligence.

And honestly?

We’re still extremely early.

どん底から這い上がる人のそばには、
必ずと言っていいほど、

「その人の本質を思い出させる存在」がいる。

それは恋人とは限らない。
夫婦とも限らない。
男性とも限らない。

友人かもしれない。
先生かもしれない。
仲間かもしれない。
家族かもしれない。
たった一言をくれた誰かかもしれない。

大切なのは、
その人があなたを小さく扱わないこと。

あなたが自分を諦めそうになった時に、
「あなたはそんな場所で終わる人じゃない」
と、静かに信じてくれること。

人は、
誰かに依存して強くなるんじゃない。

正しく見てくれる人の存在で、
本来の強さを思い出す。

だから、￼

content:
💎食べてキレイに痩せる習慣17選

1.朝に白湯を飲む → 代謝スイッチON

2.朝ごはんを抜かない → ドカ食い防止

3.毎食たんぱく質を摂る → 筋肉維持

4.野菜から食べる → 血糖値安定

5.よく噛んで食べる → 食べすぎ防止

6.発酵食品を摂る → 腸活サポート

7.水をこまめに飲む → むくみ対策

8.夜遅い食事を控える → 脂肪蓄積予防

9.甘い飲み物を減らす → 糖質カット

10.間食はナッツや果物 → 質を変える

11.腹八分目を意識 → 胃腸負担軽減

12.加工食品を減らす → むくみ対策

13.食物繊維を摂る → 腸内環境改善

14.良質な脂質を摂る → 美肌サポート

15.寝る3時間前は食べすぎない 
→ 消化負担減

16.アルコールを控えめに → むくみ防止

17.食後に少し歩く → 血糖値対策

無理なく続けて、理想の私に近づこう♡

♥完璧を目指さなくてOK！
♥小さな習慣から始めよう♪
♥ 自分を褒めてモチベUP！

title:
We launched 2 new business verticals this year.

Both worked from literally day one.

1. Two-week live bootcamps
content:
We launched 2 new business verticals this year.

Both worked from literally day one.

1. Two-week live bootcamps                                                                                                       
2. AI Writing Skool membership community

We clearly tapped into

a vein of demand for people who want to learn live, on rotating topics, and then talk about them over time within a community.

We saw massive uptake and positive response on our Bootcamp and AI Writing Skool community offers.

These felt so “smooth” that we felt stupid for not having come to the realization sooner.

I’m not saying they were easy.

They took a ton of work, effort, energy, and hours from our entire team. But that effort faced little resistance, like a knife cutting through soft butter.

And in looking back, this is true for basically every big leap in business we’ve had in the past.

So now when I feel like something is becoming forced, or the effort is not flowing smoothly, it’s a signal that I need to change my approach.

This could be either pivoting the initiative entirely, our approach to it, or the team members involved in it.

I need to spend more time bringing awareness to that, because there is no better feeling than having your entire team in alignment on something that is clearly working.

content:
Hey gang - would love your help with something:

We’re on the hunt for a growth co-founder for our software studio - and I’d love your help in finding the right person 😊

Basically: We’re building a suite of software products across productivity, personal development and the creator economy. The mission is to help 100 million people take back control of their time, energy and focus, and make progress on the goals that actually matter to them.

We’re 18 months in, bootstrapped, profitable, doing $1m+ ARR, with a large aligned audience of 10M+ across socials, 100,000+ users on one consumer product, and a B2B product already used by teams at Notion, Superhuman, Wispr Flow, Morning Brew and others. Our small team already has very strong product, engineering and design.

Our missing piece is a proper growth co-founder: double-digit equity, double-digit profit share from day one, high autonomy, fully remote, and a lot of distribution already in place.

The person we’re looking for probably isn’t a traditional VP of Growth. They’re more likely to be a hands-on, internet-native operator who’s personally made something grow recently - through content, creator partnerships, UGC, viral ads, weird internet experiments, or anything else that actually moves the needle.

If someone came to mind while reading this, please could you send them this link? https://t.co/cFSqTN3Wqf

Thank you 🙏
